sentences.text: HC-KAR  ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR) Heard the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and the learned HCGP appearing on behalf of respondent No.1,
as well as the learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2/Victim.

2. The petitioner has filed this Criminal Petition under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.') / Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, the BNSS), seeking to be enlarged on bail with the following reliefs:
"Prayer:
Wherefore, the petitioner most respectfully pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to:
1. Set aside the impugned order dated 13.10.2025 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Gadag, in SC.No.91/2025 before the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Gadag.
2. Enlarge the petitioner/Accused No.1 on Regular Bail SC No.91/2025; (Gadag Women P.S. Crime No.18/2025) for the offences punishable Under Section 6 of POCSO Act, Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 9, NC:
2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR 10, and 11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 2006, on such terms and conditions as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit;
3. Pass such other order or orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the interests of justice and equity."
3.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Gadag
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is the brief case of prosecution, as per the complaint averments that the petitioner/accused No.1 was working in water sports at Anjuna Beach, Goa, and the victim, who was minor at that time have come into close contact, developing the friendship and also compromised with each other physically at that time when the victim was minor and due to continuous cohabitation between them, the victim gave birth to a child.

Thus, the petitioner/accused No.1 committed offences punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 9,
10 and 11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 2006.

4. The victim is arrayed as respondent No.2 and Sri. P. Vadiraja, learned counsel for respondent No.2/victim NC: 2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR submitted to enlarge the petitioner on bail on the ground that PW-2/victim and the petitioner/accused No.1 have married each other and living Vinayaka S/O Chandra Shekhar Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39305986/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 together and both are having one child
; therefore, submitted to the Court to enlarge the petitioner/accused No.1 on bail, enabling both to lead marriage life.
5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner/accused No.1 submitted that the petitioner/accused No.1 is in judicial custody since 20.07.2025.

It is submitted that respondent No.2/victim while giving statement before the learned Magistrate during the investigation has not stated anything against the petitioner/accused No.1 and even after filing of the charge sheet, the trial has commenced and in the trial, the victim has given evidence stating nothing against the petitioner.
Therefore, from the examination of PW-2, who is the victim and also wife of the petitioner, nothing incriminating against NC: 2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR the petitioner/accused No.1 has been deposed.
Hence, prays to enlarge the petitioner/accused No.1 on bail.
6. On the other hand, the learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail application and prays to dismiss the petition.

7. It is the case of the prosecution that the petitioner had a relationship with the victim when the victim was minor and made her pregnant and she gave birth to a child when she was a minor girl below the age of 18 years.

The subsequent developments are that the petitioner married the victim in the presence of elders and also that the victim was giving her statement before the Police and before the learned Magistrate under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C./Section 183 of BNSS, nothing has been stated against the petitioner/accused No.1.
As per this statement of the victim given before the learned Magistrate found nothing incriminating against the petitioner/accused No.1 is revealed.

Furthermore, the victim is examined as PW-2 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR during the trial before the Sessions Court and she has stated that the petitioner/accused No.1 is her husband and the father of her child and nothing has been stated in the trial against the petitioner/accused No.1.
Therefore, in this context, learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.1 submitted that the petitioner/accused No.1 be enlarged on bail.

8. Further, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner/accused No.1 has submitted that in very similar circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has quashed the proceedings initiated against the accused and has placed reliance on the observations made in the order in the case of K.
KIRUBAKARAN VS. STATE OF TAMIL NADU1 and has brought to the notice of this Court the observations made in Paragraph No.9, which reads as follows:
2025 Live Law (SC) 1048 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR "9.

K.
KIRUBAKARAN VS. STATE OF TAMIL NADU1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Per the law made by the legislature, the appellant having been found guilty of a heinous offence,
the proceedings in the present case on the basis of a compromise between the appellant and his wife cannot be quashed.

But ignoring the cry of the appellant's wife for compassion and empathy will not,
in our opinion, serve the ends of justice.
Even the most serious offenders of law do receive justice moderated by compassion from the courts, albeit in appropriate cases.
Given the peculiar facts and circumstances here, a balanced approach combining practicality and empathy is necessary.
The appellant and the victim are not only legally married, they are also in their family way.

While considering the offence committed by the appellant punishable under the POCSO Act, we have Vinayaka S/O Chandra Shekhar Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39305986/
4 discerned that the crime was not result of lust but love.

entities.text: Vinayaka S/O Chandra Shekhar Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The victim of crime herself has expressed her desire to live a peaceful and stable family life with the appellant, upon whom she is dependent,
without the appellant carrying the indelible mark on his forehead of being an offender.

Continuation of the criminal proceedings and the appellant's incarceration would only disrupt this familial unit and cause irreparable harm to the victim, the infant child, and the fabric of society itself."
9.

Though the above stated case is for quashing and the present petition is for enlarging the petitioner on bail, considering the factors in the present case that the victim has become the wife of the petitioner/accused No.1 and has also given birth to a child and that the victim during the course of investigation, while giving her NC: 2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR statement before the learned Magistrate has deposed nothing against the petitioner/accused No.1.
Also, the victim has not stated any allegations against the petitioner/accused No.1 during the trial before the Special Court.

Hence,
considering the above factors discussed and also considering the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above said case and further considering that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 20.07.2025, I am of the opinion to enlarge the petitioner/accused No.1 on bail.

Thus,
the petition is liable to be allowed.

10. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed.

ii. The petitioner/accused No.1 is ordered to enlarge on bail in SC No.91 of 2025; (Gadag Women P.S. Crime No.18 of 2025) for the offences punishable - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3312 HC-KAR under Sections 6 of the POCSO Act, Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 9, 10 and 11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 2006, pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge, Gadag, subject to the following conditions.
